change.author: nicktrn

findings.title: A backup code plus any non-empty totpCode logs in without checking the password
findings.body: The password is checked only when `!credentials.totpCode` (line 121). Before this change that was safe, because a non-empty `totpCode` sent you into the TOTP branch, which then had to validate. Now, when `backupCode` is present, the new branch at line 131 runs and the TOTP branch is skipped. A request to the credentials provider with `email`, `totpCode: "x"` and a valid `backupCode` therefore skips both the password check and the TOTP check. A single leaked backup code becomes a full one-factor credential for the account. Fix: always verify the password in the backup-code branch, or make the line 121 condition ignore `totpCode` when `backupCode` is set (e.g. `if (user.password && (!credentials.totpCode || credentials.backupCode))`).

findings.title: Closing the backup-codes step with Escape or the overlay leaves the settings page showing 2FA as disabled
findings.body: Once enable succeeds, the modal moves to `DisplayBackupCodes` and calls `onEnable()` only from the Close button (line 269). The parent's `onOpenChange` just toggles `enableModalOpen` (apps/web/pages/settings/security/two-factor-auth.tsx:64). Dismissing the dialog with Escape or an outside click therefore never runs `utils.viewer.me.invalidate()`, so the badge and switch still say 2FA is disabled even though it is on. `resetState()` is not run either, so reopening the modal shows the old backup codes step again. Call `onEnable`/invalidate as soon as enable succeeds, or handle `onOpenChange` inside the modal so it does the same as Close.

findings.title: Using up a backup code is read-modify-write and not atomic
findings.body: The codes are read in the `findUnique` at line 73, checked in memory, and written back unconditionally. Two logins running at the same time with the same code both pass the check, so a "single-use" code can be used more than once. You could make the update conditional on the old ciphertext (`updateMany` with `where: { id, backupCodes: user.backupCodes }`, then require count === 1).

findings.title: Throwing in an API route returns a 500 with no JSON body
findings.body: Everywhere else this handler returns `res.status(500).json({ error: ErrorCode.InternalServerError })`, for example line 23. The new missing-key path throws instead, so the client gets an unstructured 500. Return the JSON error to match the rest of the handler.

findings.title: Component is named `TwoFactor`
findings.body: The default export of BackupCode.tsx is called `TwoFactor`, the same name as the component in TwoFactor.tsx. That is confusing in stack traces and React DevTools. Rename it to `BackupCode`.

contracts.before_after: Password is checked only when totpCode is empty (line 121). The TOTP path made up for that by validating totpCode. The backup branch does not, so the password is never checked when totpCode is also sent.
contracts.visible_effect: A login succeeds with a backup code and no password.
contracts.failure_mode: If the key is missing, an InternalServerError is thrown. A wrong code gives IncorrectBackupCode, which login.tsx:157 shows to the user.

contracts.action: Showing the backup codes step after enabling 2FA
contracts.equivalent_path: Previously onEnable() was called right away
contracts.before_after: onEnable, which invalidates `me`, now runs only from the Close button.
contracts.visible_effect: If the user dismisses the dialog any other way, the badge stays on 'disabled'.
contracts.failure_mode: Escape or an overlay click goes through onOpenChange (two-factor-auth.tsx:64), which only toggles the open state.

contracts.before_after: The password is still verified at lines 40-45 before the backup code is checked. The final update clears backupCodes.
contracts.visible_effect: The modal shows incorrect_backup_code or missing_backup_codes.
contracts.failure_mode: A missing key throws, which gives a raw 500.

summary: Blocker: in the credentials login, sending any non-empty totpCode together with a valid backupCode skips both the password check and the TOTP check. A single backup code is then enough to log in. Also: dismissing the backup-codes step without the Close button never calls onEnable, so the settings page shows stale state. Consider-level: the backup code is used up non-atomically, disable.ts throws a raw 500 when the encryption key is missing, and the BackupCode component is named TwoFactor.
